_meta.title: wiki-confirmed no-drop-source verdicts (#262)
_meta.note: Curated evidence shard for the 'no known live drop source' disclosure. Each entry records a per-item verdict harvested from that item's own DDO wiki page: `confirmed_no_source` means the RENDERED page's Location/acquisition reading shows no quest and no chest (verified on the rendered page, never from wikitext alone), and flags the item in the built dataset; `wiki_has_source` means the wiki records a source our data lacks (the item stays unflagged; the entry exists so re-triage skips it and the location backfill can find it). The vocabulary is CLOSED at those two verdicts: an unverified or page-missing item is NEVER written here — it lives in the docs tracker only, because this shard may only carry claims the wiki settled. The wording bar (three claim strengths, kept distinct): 'Location section empty' is the observation, 'no known live drop source' is the disclosable claim, 'unobtainable' is never claimed — the wiki proves its page records no source, not that the item cannot exist.
_meta.guard_rules: The build FAILS when (a) an entry carries a verdict outside the closed vocabulary; (b) an entry names an item absent from the planner roster (anti-orphan — renamed or dropped upstream); (c) a confirmed_no_source entry is missing its evidence snapshot, wiki_url, or harvested date; (d) STALENESS: an entry's item carries a non-empty upstream `quests` array (the raw planner list, NOT the derived location_quest string) — the wiki/gear-planner now records a source, and un-flagging is a manual review event, never automatic. An ABSENT shard or an EMPTY harvested map is fully inert (no flags, no coverage block) — the deliberate exclude-until-verified empty-seed exception; once entries exist, every guard fires and a zero-inspected pass is refused.
_meta.provenance_vocabulary: `stated` — the verdict was read off the item's own rendered wiki page (the absorption/enchantment discipline; nothing weaker is admitted here).
